Hey @pcbeingused333, thank you for your contribution!

The change looks good to me. The awaitable fix in `execute_pubsub_method` also fixes the existing async `unsubscribe`/`punsubscribe` wrappers, which never sent their commands. The sharded methods and the failover resubscription now match the sync client. I will approve the CI workflows, and once they pass this is ready to merge.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Await the actual sharded unsubscribe operation**

When callers use this method with the real asyncio PubSub, `redis.asyncio.client.PubSub.sunsubscribe` is a regular `def` that returns an `Awaitable`, but `DefaultCommandExecutor.execute_pubsub_method` (`redis/asyncio/multidb/command_executor.py:272-283`) only awaits methods recognized as coroutine functions. Consequently the single `await` here resolves to the inner coroutine object without sending `SUNSUBSCRIBE`, leaving the server subscription active while failure detection records success; await returned awaitables in the executor so this API behaves like its synchronous counterpart.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L146-L149](https://github.com/redis/redis-py/blob/28f2780adc56760ce4bc9f04f56adae3e68b30b4/AGENTS.md#L146-L149)

### Sharded unsubscribe never sends command **High Severity** Calling `sunsubscribe` does not send `SUNSUBSCRIBE` to Redis. `execute_pubsub_method` only awaits coroutine functions, but the underlying `sunsubscribe` is a regular method that returns an awaitable, so the command is never executed and the subscription stays active.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate shard handlers before starting `run`**

For a standalone MultiDB PubSub, when a caller uses the newly exposed positional form (`await ps.ssubscribe("c")`) and then starts `ps.run()`, `redis/asyncio/client.py:1791-1808` validates only `channels`/`patterns` and consumes each returned message without using it, so every `smessage` is silently lost. The sync path explicitly checks `shard_channels` and raises `PubSubError` (`redis/client.py:1786-1790`); add the same check before the async run loop so the new surface preserves that contract, as required by the repository's sync/async parity rule.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align `sunsubscribe` argument types across stacks**

For users type-checking the mirrored MultiDB APIs, this new async method constrains every argument to `ChannelT`, while the sync counterpart at `redis/multidb/client.py:758` exposes untyped `*args`, so switching stacks changes checker behavior for the same public call. Give both declarations the same argument type to satisfy the repository requirement that sync and async type hints remain identical.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the sharded timeout type across stacks**

For callers passing the documented `None` timeout, the new async signature accepts `Optional[float]` while the sync counterpart at `redis/multidb/client.py:783-785` declares only `float`, so the same valid call is type-checked differently between clients. Align both as `float | None`, which also follows the repository's required PEP 604 style and sync/async type parity.

Fixed in 7138f587: the asyncio `sunsubscribe` now takes untyped `*args`, like its sync counterpart.

The new method follows the existing asyncio `get_message` in the same class, which already declares `Optional[float]` while the sync one declares `float`. Aligning both stacks would change the sync signatures too, so I left it out of this PR; happy to do it here or separately if you prefer.
